title: Design LRU Cache with O(1) Operations
question: Design an LRU (Least Recently Used) cache that supports get() and put() operations in O(1) time complexity. The cache should have a fixed capacity. When the cache reaches its capacity and a new key-value pair needs to be inserted, the least recently used item should be evicted. Explain your choice of data structures and provide the complete implementation with thread-safety considerations for a multi-threaded environment where multiple threads might access the cache concurrently.
realWorldScenario: Building production-grade caching system with O(1) operations

title: Design Time-Based Key-Value Store
question: Design a time-based key-value data structure that can store multiple values for the same key at different timestamps and retrieve the key's value at a certain timestamp. The store should support: 1) set(key, value, timestamp) - stores the key with value at the given timestamp, 2) get(key, timestamp) - returns the value for key at timestamp, or the most recent value if exact timestamp doesn't exist. The system handles 100M+ entries with frequent reads and writes. Optimize for fast retrieval. Discuss data structures, time complexity, and how to handle memory constraints.
realWorldScenario: Building time-series data store for historical lookups

title: Find Median from Data Stream
question: You're building a real-time analytics system that processes a continuous stream of transaction amounts. The system needs to provide the median transaction amount at any point in time. New transactions arrive at a rate of 10,000 per second. The median query can happen at any time and must return results in under 10ms. Design a data structure that efficiently maintains the median as new elements arrive. Discuss the time complexity for both insertion and median retrieval operations, and explain how you would handle the high throughput requirements.
realWorldScenario: Real-time median calculation for streaming data

title: Design Real-Time Top K Frequent Elements System
question: Design a system for a social media platform that tracks trending topics in real-time. The system receives millions of events per minute (each event is a topic/hashtag). You need to provide the top 100 trending topics at any moment. The trending score is based on frequency in the last 15 minutes (sliding window). Old events should automatically expire. The system must handle: 1) addEvent(topic, timestamp), 2) getTopK(k) returning the top k topics. Optimize for: fast insertion, fast top-k retrieval, automatic expiration. Discuss data structures, time complexity, memory usage, and how to handle late-arriving events.
realWorldScenario: Building real-time trending/top-k system with sliding window

title: Design Autocomplete System with Ranking
question: Design an autocomplete system for a search engine with 50 million search queries in the database. As users type, the system should suggest the top 10 most popular completions in under 50ms. Each query has an associated frequency (how many times it was searched). The system should support: 1) input(character) - takes next character and returns top 10 suggestions, 2) updateFrequency(query, count) - updates search frequency. Discuss the optimal data structure (Trie with ranking?), how to maintain top-k at each node efficiently, memory optimization techniques for storing 50M queries, and how to handle typo tolerance.
realWorldScenario: Building fast autocomplete with ranking and large dataset

title: Detect Fraud Patterns in Transaction Stream
question: Design a fraud detection system for a payment processor that analyzes transaction streams in real-time. The system needs to detect suspicious patterns: 1) Same card used at geographically distant locations within a short time (velocity check), 2) Unusual spending pattern (sudden large transactions), 3) Multiple failed attempts followed by success. Transactions arrive at 5,000/sec. Each transaction has: card_id, amount, merchant, location, timestamp. The system must flag suspicious transactions in under 100ms. Discuss the data structures for: tracking recent transactions per card, detecting geographic anomalies, maintaining spending profiles, and efficiently querying time-windowed data.
realWorldScenario: Real-time fraud detection with multiple pattern checks

title: Merge K Sorted Streams with Memory Constraints
question: Your distributed system has K worker nodes (K=1000), each producing a sorted stream of log entries by timestamp. You need to merge these streams into a single sorted output stream for a central logging system. Constraints: 1) Each worker produces 100 logs/sec, 2) System memory can only buffer 10,000 log entries total, 3) Output must maintain timestamp order, 4) Minimize latency (emit logs as soon as possible). Which data structure would you use? Discuss time complexity, space complexity, how to handle slow/failed workers, backpressure handling, and how to minimize the latency between log generation and output.
realWorldScenario: Merging multiple sorted streams with memory limits

title: Design Real-Time Route Optimization System
question: Design a routing system for a ride-sharing app that finds the shortest path between pickup and drop-off locations in real-time. The road network has 1 million intersections and 3 million road segments. Road conditions change dynamically (traffic, closures). The system needs to: 1) find optimal route in under 500ms, 2) handle 10,000 concurrent route requests, 3) incorporate real-time traffic updates every 30 seconds. Discuss: graph representation, which shortest path algorithm (Dijkstra? A*? bidirectional?), how to handle dynamic weight updates efficiently, pre-computation strategies, and how to scale for a city with millions of nodes.
realWorldScenario: Building real-time routing with dynamic graph weights

title: Design Distributed Rate Limiter with Sliding Window
question: Design a distributed rate limiter for an API gateway that limits requests per user: max 100 requests per minute using a sliding window algorithm. The system has 10 API gateway instances (not centralized). Requirements: 1) Accurate rate limiting (not exceeding 100 even with race conditions), 2) Reject excess requests immediately, 3) Handle 1 million active users, 4) Sub-millisecond latency for rate check. Discuss: data structures for tracking request timestamps, how to implement sliding window efficiently, memory optimization (can't store all timestamps), handling distributed coordination, and the trade-off between accuracy and performance.
realWorldScenario: Building distributed rate limiter with sliding window

title: Design Real-Time Gaming Leaderboard at Scale
question: Design a leaderboard system for a multiplayer game with 10 million players. Requirements: 1) Update player score (can happen 10 times/sec per player during active gameplay), 2) Get player's current rank, 3) Get top 100 players globally, 4) Get players around a specific rank (rank ± 50). All operations must complete in under 50ms. Scores can only increase. The system needs to handle 100,000 concurrent score updates. Discuss: optimal data structure for rank queries, how to maintain global rankings efficiently, handling ties, sharding strategy for horizontal scaling, and consistency trade-offs.
realWorldScenario: Building high-performance real-time leaderboard at scale
